children: Asian equities fluctuated between gains and losses Thursday afternoon as investors weighed a pause in the global bond selloff, while the yen strengthened to nearly a four-week high against the dollar.

Comments from New York Fed President John Williams in an interview with CNBC on Wednesday soothed concerns over an imminent interest-rate increase by the Federal Reserve, providing a lift to sentiment in equity and bond markets. Williams indicated that he doesn't see clear-cut evidence currently that the Fed must lift interest rates to respond to persistent inflation.

He described U.S. interest rates as "in a good place" and signaled a wait‑and‑see approach ahead of the Fed's meeting later this month, said Kristina Clifton, a senior economist and currency strategist at Commonwealth Bank of Australia, in a research report.
Williams is the No. 2 member of the Federal Reserve's rate-setting committee and has often represented the thinking of Fed officials near the center of the policy debate.
"Fed funds futures modestly reduced rate hike expectations to 37.8bp of tightening for this year, compared with 40bp earlier in the week," OCBC Group Research's global markets team said in a note.

South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei Stock Average swung between gains and losses throughout the Asian session, and were last 0.3% higher and 0.1% lower, respectively. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index edged 0.3% lower while China's Shanghai Composite edged 0.1% higher. Malaysia's FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI added 0.1% and Singapore's FTSE Straits Times Index was little changed.
The yen strengthened against the dollar and other currencies amid prospects for more aggressive monetary-policy tightening by the Bank of Japan as early as this month's meeting.

The Bank of Japan has remained in focus, UOB's Global Economics & Markets Research team said in a research report. In a speech on Wednesday, "hawkish [BOJ] board member Hajime Takata left the door open for an outsized rate increase and back-to-back hikes," the team said. Takata also said that a 25-basis-point rate increase "is not necessarily set in stone," the team noted.
The dollar slipped 0.9% to 157.34 yen after earlier touching 157.23 yen, the lowest intraday level since Aug. 7, according to LSEG data.

Yields on Japan's 10-year government bonds fell 4.5 basis points to 2.965% after touching a three-decade high of 3.015% on Wednesday. Yields on Australia's two-year and 10-year sovereign securities were down 6 basis points and 5 basis points, respectively, at 4.7750% and 5.1510%. Bond yields move inversely to prices.

Crude oil futures declined in Asia after closing higher overnight for a third consecutive session. However, losses could be limited by ongoing worries over further escalation in strikes between the U.S. and Iran and disruptions to oil flows out of the Middle East.
Front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil futures declined 1.1% to $90.00 a barrel and front-month Brent crude oil futures fell 1.3% to $94.37 a barrel, according to ICE data.
